newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bridge collapses at Israeli sports event, 1 killed.
newsitem.headline: Bridge collapses at Israeli sports event, 1 killed.

text.p: A bridge at an Israeli sports stadium collapsed just before the opening ceremonies of an international Jewish sporting event, killing one person and injuring 18, police said.
The pedestrian bridge, over a body of water, collapsed at the Ramat Gan stadium near Tel Aviv where the quadrennial Maacabiah Games -- nicknamed the "Jewish Olympics" -- were due to begin.
Police said one person was killed and 18 were injured, three of them seriously.
Israel Television showed a bag with a body in it.
The television said many of the 370-member Australia delegation were standing on the bridge preparing to enter the stadium at the start of a parade of national teams when the bridge collapsed.
Organisers cancelled the march but went ahead with the opening ceremonies for the games which bring together Jewish athletes from all over the world.
Some 40 minutes after the collapse of the bridge, Israeli President Ezer Weizman declared the games open.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was due to attend the opening ceremonies but his office said they did not believe he was anywhere near the bridge when it collapsed.
"A pedestrian bridge next to the Ramat Gan Stadium collapsed. There are many injured who have been evacuated to hospitals. There are seriously injured," police said in a statement.

Harry Purcell, the Australia team manager, told reporters: "We were walking across. All of a sudden we heard a bang. It was like a loud noise. And then all of a sudden in slow motion it just collapsed in the middle and we started to slide."

One of the Australian delegation members, Ari Kochmalik, told the television: "I was on the bridge. There were a lot of people on the bridge and the bridge fell. That's what happened. And there was water under the bridge and there are a number of people who fell in the water.
"I fell in the water and suddenly I felt air, thank God, but I don't know what happened to the other people," he said.
It was not immediately clear what caused the bridge to collapse. There was no immediate suggestion of foul play.

Israel Television broadcast pictures of Netanyahu's security men scrambling amidst ambulances rushing to help wounded. Ambulances carried away wounded while stunned spectators watched from the packed stadium.
